headline: What to Consider When Enlarging Your Pantry
articleBody: Deciding to enlarge your pantry is a fantastic move for boosting kitchen efficiency and storage, but there are a few things you'll want to mull over before you start. It's not just about adding shelves; it’s about creating a truly functional space. First, really take stock of what you plan to store. Are we talking dry goods, small appliances, bulky items, or a mix of everything? This will impact your shelving needs – depth, adjustability, and load capacity are all key. While 12-inch deep shelves work for many items, going too deep, especially beyond 18 inches, can actually hide things and make them hard to reach. Also, think about lighting and ventilation. A well-lit pantry prevents forgotten items, and good ventilation keeps things fresh. Don't forget about door swings and aisle clearances! You want to be able to comfortably access everything without bumping into shelves or other people. Lastly, consider any structural implications. If you're removing or opening walls, or adding new electrical for appliances, that's definitely a cue to bring in a professional.
